title: Security posture discovery - Aurora Genomics
summary: Initial security posture discovery focused on hosted vs dedicated vs private deployment for sensitive genomics workloads. Discussed SOC 2/ISO requirements, SSO/SAML, RBAC, audit logs, encryption/KMS integration, data residency and retention policies. Team requested SOC2 report, threat model doc, and a week-of-demo to run an isolated inference benchmark in Dedicated/VPC. Agreed next steps and action items.
topics: Encryption at rest and KMS integration

Schedule dedicated/VPC proof-of-concept demo for week of Mar 14
Provide pricing/seat and Dedicated capacity options to Samir

transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2027-03-03
Time: 14:00 - 14:48 UTC
Duration: ~48 minutes
Attendees: Liam Chen (Redwood AE), Maya Rodriguez (Redwood SE), Dr. Elena Park (CISO, Aurora Genomics), Marcus Lee (Head of Platform), Nina O'Connor (DevOps), Samir Patel (Product), Kelly Tran (Legal)

[00:00] Liam Chen: Hi everyone, thanks for joining. I'm Liam from Redwood, this is Maya, our solutions engineer. Quick intro round, then we'll dive into your security posture and what you're looking for for hosting models, is that right?

[00:18] Dr. Elena Park: Yep, thanks. I'm Elena, CISO at Aurora. We're evaluating options — hosted, dedicated, or private — for an LLM-based ingestion pipeline for genomic annotations. Biggest concerns are data residency, key management, and retention. Also need SOC2 evidence.

[00:35] Liam Chen: Totally, understood. Maya, do you want to kick off with how Redwood handles compliance and deployment modes?

[00:42] Maya Rodriguez: Sure. So high level: our Hosted API is fast to get started and has multi-tenant isolation, we have SOC 2 Type II and ISO attestations for the control plane. For stronger isolation and predictable throughput we offer Dedicated, which is reserved GPU pools with isolated tenancy, and Private deployments run in a customer VPC or on-prem. Each mode has different controls around network access, key management, and log ownership.

[01:10] Marcus Lee: Quick question — when you say SOC2 and ISO, do you provide the actual report or just an attestation? Legal will want to see the report.

[01:17] Liam Chen: We can share the SOC 2 Type II report under an NDA; we'll make that available to Kelly. Also have ISO 27001 attestation. We'll put those in the folder.

[01:25] Kelly Tran: Great. We'll need the detailed scope — which systems and regions are covered, especially any third-party subprocessors and where logs are stored.

[01:34] Maya Rodriguez: Absolutely. Our SOC2 covers our control plane and hosted data handling processes; for Dedicated and Private, control shifts more to the customer's environment — you run the nodes or we dedicate them to you, and you control the network boundary.

[01:48] Nina O'Connor: For Dedicated, who holds the encryption keys? We want to use our KMS and ensure keys are customer-managed.

[01:56] Maya Rodriguez: For Dedicated you can bring your own KMS — we integrate with AWS KMS, GCP KMS, and customer HSMs in Private environments. For Hosted, we manage keys by default but offer envelope encryption and narrow key separation; we can discuss VPC peering plus a KMS proxy if you need customer-managed keys.

[02:16] Dr. Elena Park: Is there support for HSM-backed keys? We have regulatory constraints for some genotyping outputs.

[02:22] Liam Chen: Yes, on Private deployments we can support HSM integration and a customer-managed KMS/HSM. We'll outline architecture patterns in the doc we send.

[02:30] [brief cross talk] Samir Patel: Are there any known limitations on tokenization or model caching that would inadvertently keep PHI or PII in caches? We need guarantee that sensitive strings from genomic IDs don't persist.

[02:42] Maya Rodriguez: Good question. We have KV cache management and prefix caching that can be disabled; for dedicated and private setups we give you control over cache lifetime and deletion. Also our recommended pattern for regulated workloads is Dedicated within a VPC with KV cache disabled or cleared after the session, plus strict RBAC.

[03:05] Marcus Lee: Speaking of RBAC, how granular is it? Can we separate dev/test/admin and restrict model rollback or access to logs?

[03:13] Maya Rodriguez: Our RBAC supports role definitions (admin, ops, readonly, support) and you can create custom roles. We integrate with SSO via SAML/SCIM so you can map your IdP groups. For Dedicated and Private, you control the console access boundary and logs.

[03:32] Dr. Elena Park: We need SSO and SCIM with our Okta setup, plus session expiry policies. Can you enforce session timeouts and MFA through our IdP?

[03:40] Liam Chen: Yes — we delegate auth to the IdP via SAML/OIDC, so MFA/session policies are enforced by Okta. We just validate tokens. We also support SCIM for provisioning.

[03:49] Nina O'Connor: How about audit logs — do we get syslog forwarding or CloudWatch/Stackdriver export? We want immutable logs for 12 months, and integration with our SIEM.

[03:59] Maya Rodriguez: We provide audit logs for API calls, admin actions, and model rollouts. For Hosted we retain logs per our retention policy but can forward to your SIEM via secure log export (S3/CloudWatch/Push). For Dedicated and Private you can retain logs in your environment with your retention controls. We can support WORM-like storage if needed.

[04:25] Dr. Elena Park: Is there a way to get signed audit artifacts for compliance review?

[04:30] Liam Chen: We can provide signed event logs and a chain-of-custody document for Dedicated/Private POCs. For Hosted we'll provide exportable logs and attestations tied to the SOC2 scope.

[04:42] Marcus Lee: On data residency — our data must remain in the EU region for a subset of workloads. Do you have region pinning or EU-only tenancy?

[04:50] Maya Rodriguez: Yes, we have region pinning and EU-only hosting options. For Dedicated you can reserve capacity in specific cloud regions, and Private allows you to deploy inside your EU VPC. We'll capture the exact regions in the POC notes.

[05:05] Samir Patel: For the POC, we want to test both latency and cost at our expected QPS, and validate that no raw payloads are retained. What's the usual approach?

[05:15] Maya Rodriguez: We typically do a short benchmark: deploy a Dedicated GPU pool in your VPC, run your sample payload at scaled QPS, enable audit logging and disable caching to validate no retention. We'll capture end-to-end traces and cost per token under your profile.

[05:29] Nina O'Connor: We'll need a checklist so DevOps can run this internally too.

[05:34] Lily Chen: (note: speaker mislabel) sorry, Liam —

[05:36] Liam Chen: (laughs) that's me. We'll send a benchmark checklist along with the KMS and network diagrams.

[05:43] Kelly Tran: On legal side, what's your data retention policy for logs and model inputs for Hosted by default? Does Redwood keep prompts for model training or improvement? We need explicit contract language that no customer prompts are used for model training without opt-in.

[05:58] Maya Rodriguez: We do not train on customer prompts by default. We retain request/response logs for a configurable period for debugging and billing; default retention for Hosted is 90 days, but we can set shorter or forward/expire logs per customer contract. We'll provide contract language and options.

[06:14] Dr. Elena Park: We also want assurance on how long ephemeral compute caches hold data. Is there a guaranteed TTL and secure deletion process?

[06:22] Maya Rodriguez: For Dedicated/Private deployments you control KV cache TTL; we can configure zero retention for KV caches, and we have secure deletion procedures for disk volumes and ephemeral memory — we'll include our sanitization process in the security pack.

[06:36] Marcus Lee: Encryption in transit and at rest? TLS versions supported? FIPS?

[06:42] Liam Chen: TLS 1.2 and 1.3 supported, we support AES-256 at rest. For FIPS/HSM requirements we advise Private with HSM-backed keys — that matches your regulatory needs.

[06:55] Samir Patel: Any third-party subprocessors or cloud vendors we should flag for procurement?

[07:00] Maya Rodriguez: We use cloud providers (AWS/GCP) and a few managed infra providers — list of subprocessors will be in the compliance pack.

[07:08] Kelly Tran: We'll need a subprocessors list and SOC2 carve-outs if any.

[07:14] Liam Chen: We'll include the subprocessors and the scoped controls.

[07:19] Nina O'Connor: On network isolation — if we do Dedicated in our VPC, is there a way to block outbound access from the inference nodes to the internet?

[07:27] Maya Rodriguez: Yes — for Private/VPC deployments you can control egress rules; we can provision NATless configurations or require egress proxy to monitor traffic.

[07:36] Dr. Elena Park: For incident response, what's your SLA and notification process? Will Redwood notify our security team and provide raw logs in case of suspected data exposure?

[07:46] Liam Chen: We have incident response procedures and can include customers in the notification loop. For Dedicated/Private you get full log access. We also offer an IR runbook exchange to align on escalation paths; we'll include that in the pack.

[07:58] Samir Patel: Cost question — if we go Dedicated with reserved capacity, can we burst to additional GPUs for spikes?

[08:06] Maya Rodriguez: Yes, Dedicated supports configurable burst policies. We'll outline typical commit vs burst pricing in the pricing doc.

[08:14] Marcus Lee: Any limitations on model versions in Dedicated? For instance quantized variants or Llama-2 forks?

[08:21] Maya Rodriguez: We support a curated model catalog and can bring customer models for Private/Dedicated. Quantized variants are supported and we'll include recommended quantization profiles for your workload.

[08:33] Dr. Elena Park: Ok — this is helpful. Can you put together the following: SOC2/ISO reports, subprocessors list, KMS/HSM integration guide, network/VPC diagrams, POC benchmark checklist, and contract language about data not being used for training?

[08:48] Liam Chen: Yes — action items we'll capture: Liam to send SOC2 and ISO, Maya to send KMS diagrams and POC plan, we'll schedule a POC demo week of Mar 14. Kelly, you'll review compliance docs.

[09:02] Kelly Tran: Sounds good. We'll also need to coordinate an NDA for the SOC2 report.

[09:08] Liam Chen: We'll surface an NDA link in the email.

[09:12] [pause]

[09:15] Maya Rodriguez: One technical nit — when you run the benchmark, disable training telemetry and set request retention to zero, then run your payload for the desired QPS. We'll collect latency, p95/p99, token cost and trace logs.

[09:29] Nina O'Connor: We'll draft a sample payload and expected QPS by Friday.

[09:33] Dr. Elena Park: A few follow-ups from policy — do you support data subject access requests (DSAR) handling if someone requests deletion of their data?

[09:41] Liam Chen: For Hosted, we have processes to locate and delete request logs within retention windows; for Dedicated/Private, you'll have control to delete data in your environment and we can provide APIs and procedures.

[09:52] Samir Patel: Anything else on encryption key rotation? We want automatic rotation but with customer control.

[09:58] Maya Rodriguez: Rotation can be managed in your KMS; we support key rotation policies and re-encryption flows. We'll document recommended rotation cadence.

[10:07] [wrap-up] Liam Chen: Quick recap — we'll send SOC2/ISO under NDA, subprocessors list, KMS/HSM guide, POC checklist and network diagrams. We'll schedule a Dedicated/VPC demo week of Mar 14 to run benchmarks. Action items assigned. Anything else?

[10:26] Kelly Tran: Please include contract language explicitly stating you won't train on customer data without opt-in. Also include specifics on log retention defaults and options.

[10:34] Liam Chen: Noted. We'll get those in the packet.

[10:38] Dr. Elena Park: Thanks everyone. Looking forward to the docs and the POC.

[10:42] Liam Chen: Thanks all. We'll follow up with calendar invites and the NDA link.

End of call.

Notes about transcript quality: auto-transcription had occasional mislabels and speaker name jitter (some speaker lines labeled with similar names). We preserved filler words and brief crosstalk.
